title: PR-level lightweight load sampler for tokens/sec p95 gating
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight synthetic workload sampler that runs on PR check pipelines to provide fast, low-cost signals for tokens/sec (throughput) and p95 latency regressions. The goal is to enable early detection of performance regressions without running full heavy benchmarks for every PR.

Motivation: Full baseline CI benchmarks are expensive and slow; we need an intermediate check that is predictive of larger regression risk. This ticket implements a compact samplers that exercises the runtime hot paths (KV cache warm-up, batching hot-path, short/medium/long sequence lengths) and produces per-model KPIs and a small fingerprint to compare against historical baselines.

Scope: - Small synthetic runner (<10s wallclock) integrated as a check in PR workflows. - Produces tokens/sec, p95 latency, and trace-level tags for sequence-length buckets. - Stores snapshot artifacts (JSON) with fingerprint and sampling variance. - Implements paired-sample statistical test (bootstrap + delta CI) against the baseline snapshot for the target model. - Fails PR gate on statistically-significant degradation beyond configurable thresholds (default: p95 worse by >10% and tokens/sec worse by >12% with p < 0.05).
acceptance_criteria:
1) PR check included in dockerized CI job that completes within the PR job timeout (<=10 minutes) and costs <0.1 core GPU-minute equivalent.
2) The sampler outputs a JSON artifact with fields: model, commit_sha, sampling_seed, sequence_buckets, tokens_per_sec_mean, tokens_per_sec_p95, p95_ci, baseline_snapshot_ref, fingerprint_hash.
3) A baseline snapshot is created for at least one production model and stored in the artifacts bucket.
4) The PR job compares the artifact to the baseline using the paired bootstrap method; the job marks the PR as failed when configured thresholds are exceeded.
5) Dashboard shows sampler runs and delta distributions; historically-known benign noise is visible.
6) Unit tests for the statistical comparator and an end-to-end smoke test in ephemeral runner complete reliably.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions and trade-offs: 1) Use short synthetic prompts derived from real workload distributions to simulate representative KV/cache behavior; avoid replaying PII or customer data. 2) Sampling size: default 64 sequences across three length buckets (short/medium/long) with adaptive early-stop if variance is low to save time. 3) Statistical method: paired bootstrap to handle non-normal latency distributions; compute 95% bootstrap CI for p95 delta and for tokens/sec. 4) Failure policy: conservative thresholds and require at least N=3 consecutive PR-based failures or a full benchmark confirmation before auto-blocking release branches. 5) Artifacts retention: sampler snapshots retained for 90 days, baseline snapshots pinned per-release.

Implementation steps: - Build sampler binary that uses the same inference client as e2e harness but runs in synthetic mode. - Add job definition to .github/workflows/pr-perf-sampler.yml. - Implement comparator library in repo/perf/checks with local test harness. - Add CI artifact uploader and baseline store access with RBAC. - Wire to PR status checks with human-facing explanation on failure and a link to the detailed diff report.
test_plan:
1) Unit tests for sampler generation and statistical comparator (CI).
2) Integration: run against canary baseline for two models (small and medium) in staging; validate that sampler reproduces known deltas from previous runs.
3) Noise injection tests: artificially add latency to runtime path and ensure sampler flags degradation with expected sensitivity.
4) Nondeterminism tests: run the sampler 30x and ensure variance metrics are within expected envelope.
5) Run end-to-end PR check on a test branch and confirm artifact creation, comparison, and dashboard ingestion.
6) Post-launch: monitor false positives for two sprints and adjust thresholds / sample sizes as needed.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (staging): run sampler as optional check for a subset of repos for 2 weeks. Collect false positive/negative metrics.
Phase 2 (soft-gate): enable as optional required check for non-release branches; block if confirmed by full benchmark.
Phase 3 (hard-gate for critical models): enable PR blocking for runtime-critical repos if sampler shows sustained regressions and full-bench confirms.
Fallback: allow auto-bypass label and a triage run (full benchmark) when a PR is blocked; provide clear runbook for triage.
progress_updates:
2025-02-10: Ticket created; initial spec shared.
2025-02-11: Prototype load-sampler binary implemented; smoke-run completes in 22s on a small test VM. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4826.
2025-02-12: Implemented bootstrap comparator and artifact schema; added unit tests for comparator.
2025-02-14: Integrated sampler into GitHub workflow and uploaded first baseline snapshot for model:rw-medium-v1. Ran 10 experimental PR checks; observed expected sensitivity to injected 15% latency increase.
Next: tune sequence bucket sizes and finalize default thresholds based on noise analysis.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: False positives due to noisy infra or small sample sizes. Mitigation: conservative thresholds, require repeat failures, and provide 'full benchmark confirm' step.
Risk: Sampler could be gamed by changes that optimize for sampler but not real traffic. Mitigation: sample prompts derived from workload distribution and have rotating prompt sets.
Risk: Additional CI time impacting developer velocity. Mitigation: keep runtime small (<2m typical), run on lightweight infra, and allow opt-out for doc-only PRs via label.
notes:
- Consider future integration with PR blame bot to attribute the likely PR diff regions correlated with perf regressions.
- Follow-up ticket: auto-trigger reduced full-bench on suspected regressions to provide stronger evidence before blocking.
- Discuss on eng-perf sync (2025-02-18) to finalize thresholds and retention policy.
